the_seats_were_wrong_about_one_thing: ⚠ R7-B4's ARITHMETIC WAS RE-DERIVED AND THE SEATS' RANGE DID NOT SURVIVE. Two seats independently reported that a third cohort of 7–8 zero-death TAF15 patients gives a pooled point estimate of '30.4–36.4 %'. Recomputed from the artifact's own counts (7 events / 15) with the generator's own wilson(): 31.8 % at +7 and 30.4 % at +8. 36.4 % corresponds to 8 events over 22, not 7 — so the upper end of their range is not a projection of this contrast at all. Their CONCLUSION was right and load-bearing (the falsifier is unreachable by the study describing it, k = 19, n ≥ 34, which reproduced exactly); one of their numbers was not. This is precisely why paper-hardening §5 forbids pasting a verifier's figures.

third_process_defect.what: ⛔ TaskStop KILLS THE HARNESS'S WRAPPER AND LEAVES `preflight.sh` RUNNING. §6 says to kill a gate the tree moved under rather than sit through it; this cycle did that three times and every TaskStop reported success. `ps` then showed the stopped run's preflight.sh still alive at 3:05 with its own `pytest -n 4`, racing the live run's — two gates, eight workers, on a four-worker box.
third_process_defect.how_it_was_found: NOT by a crash. The live gate simply overran its measured ~255 s, and CLAUDE.md §4's 'unexpected slowness is a signal, investigate rather than reassure' is the only reason anybody ran `ps`. Two prior cycles' worth of slow gates may have had the same cause and been read as 'the suite is slow today'.
third_process_defect.second_trap_confirmed_twice: The harness reports each killed run as `failed with exit code 1`, which reads exactly like a RED GATE. Seen twice in this cycle, for pf5 and pf6, both of which I had killed deliberately. Neither wrote an `EXIT=` marker — that absence is what distinguishes a killed run from a failed one, and it is precisely why the marker rule exists. This is the same class as the incident behind that rule (a harness reporting 0 for a preflight whose marker said 1), arriving from the other direction.
third_process_defect.fix_proposed: Have preflight.sh record its own pid and add `scripts/stop-preflight.sh` to kill that pid's process GROUP, or run the gate under `setsid`/`exec` so the tracked process IS the gate. ⛔ NOT `pkill -f preflight` — CLAUDE.md §6 records that pattern matching the killer's own command line three times in one session. Killed by recorded PID here.

fourth_process_defect.id: caught by an existing guard; no new instrument needed
fourth_process_defect.what: ⛔ THE ROUND-8 COMMIT (8a92d44) SHIPPED AN ARCHIVE MANIFEST POINTING AT AN ORPHANED COMMIT, AND I PUSHED IT. The manifest records the git revision it was generated at. It was regenerated at 59e068a6 — this cycle's claim commit — and then origin/main moved under the push, the rebase rewrote 59e068a6 into 1b79dd0, and the manifest's provenance line was left naming a commit reachable from no branch and no tag. A reader cloning the repository could not resolve the deposit's own provenance.
fourth_process_defect.how_it_was_found: `test_the_manifest_revision_is_a_commit_a_reader_can_resolve` failed on the NEXT preflight, and its message diagnosed the mechanism outright: 'This is what a rebase after regeneration looks like. Regenerate the manifest AFTER the final rebase.' ⭐ THAT IS WHAT A GOOD GUARD MESSAGE BUYS — the failure named its own cause and its own remedy, and cost one regeneration instead of an investigation.
fourth_process_defect.consequence_stated_plainly: CI on 8a92d44 is expected to be RED on this one test, because the defect is in the pushed commit. It is fixed forward by the follow-up commit rather than by rewriting pushed history.
fourth_process_defect.the_ordering_lesson: The regeneration chain ran BEFORE the final rebase. Any artifact that records a git revision must be regenerated after the last rebase, which means after the push is known to fast-forward — not merely before the commit. ⚠ Nothing enforces that ordering; the guard catches the result on the next run, one commit late.
